scope: Hostile audit of transferring impurity-particle contact loss to Mg/La inoculant residues in LiMgLa|LLZTO

claims.exact_statement: Ji et al. nominally use Li97.5(Mg-1 wt% La)2.5, corresponding to about 2.475 wt% Mg and 0.025 wt% La from the master alloy; the recipe does not directly provide the Vema particle volume fraction f.
claims.source: Ji et al., Supplementary Fig. 10, DOI 10.1038/s41563-026-02729-w
assumptions: the 2.5 subscript is wt% Mg-1 wt% La master alloy, as stated in the figure caption
costs: phase fraction and densities must be measured before converting mass recipe to particle volume fraction
claims.falsifier: A different author-defined composition basis or direct source characterization linking nominal recipe to volume fraction would supersede the arithmetic.
claims.next_gate: Measure phase identity, phase mass/volume fraction, size distribution, and spatial partitioning in the exact alloy.

claims.exact_statement: If all nominal La were present as LaMg3, La stoichiometry caps that phase at approximately 0.038 wt% of the alloy by mass; this is not an estimate of actual phase content and does not bound other Mg-rich phases.
claims.source: Ji et al., Supplementary Fig. 10 composition and Supplementary Fig. 21 LaMg3 candidate phase, DOI 10.1038/s41563-026-02729-w
assumptions: all nominal La is in LaMg3
no La loss or other La-bearing phases
costs: does not supply volume fraction; density and phase measurements remain necessary
claims.falsifier: A changed alloy loading, La concentration, or phase stoichiometry changes the ceiling.

claims.exact_statement: Ji Supplementary Note 4 reports broadly uniform Mg/La distribution in deposited Li without obvious segregation and retention as nucleation sites in a 4 M LiFSI/DME control; this is not an LLZTO interface capture or conductance measurement.
claims.source: Ji et al., Supplementary Note 4, DOI 10.1038/s41563-026-02729-w
costs: liquid-electrolyte control and solid-electrolyte full-strip state are not interchangeable
claims.falsifier: New protocol-matched phase-resolved data could establish a different distribution or transport role.
claims.next_gate: Map exact Mg-bearing phase and mass balance through stripping in LiMgLa|LLZTO.

claims.exact_statement: Ji Supplementary Fig. 13 maps Mg/La after partial stripping to 2 mAh cm-2; after full stripping, the figure shows SEM morphology labeled as a small grain at the interface and another in the bulk, without Mg/La EDX at that full-strip state.
claims.source: Ji et al., Supplementary Fig. 13, DOI 10.1038/s41563-026-02729-w
assumptions: published caption and panels are read literally
costs: feature chemistry at full strip remains inferred, not directly mapped
claims.falsifier: A supplementary full-state chemical map not included in the inspected figure would change this evidence boundary.
claims.next_gate: Acquire phase-resolved chemistry maps at the exact full-strip interface.

claims.exact_statement: Vema et al. report an oxygen-enriched Li-side layer after stripping against Al-LLZO and model it as insulating impurity particles deposited during stripping; the exact residue chemistry and LiMgLa transfer are not established.
claims.status: SOURCE_REPORTED mechanism with chemical identity unresolved
claims.source: Vema et al., Joule 2026, DOI 10.1016/j.joule.2026.102539 and Supplementary Fig. S2/Eqs. S18-S25
assumptions: particle-deposition/creep interpretation in their Li|Al-LLZO system
costs: f, a, a0, Z0, pressure/current-dependent critical gap, and creep parameters are source-specific
claims.falsifier: Matched LiMgLa|LLZTO measurements contradicting deposition, blocking, or pressure dependence would falsify transfer for that protocol.
claims.next_gate: Measure these parameters in the candidate anode/electrolyte system.

claims.exact_statement: For a fixed Vema sphere/gap/creep model, if only a fraction eta of the seed phase enters the contact-blocking state, replacing f by eta*f makes critical capacity scale as 1/eta; eta is unmeasured for LiMgLa.
claims.status: DERIVED conditional sensitivity/counterexample, not a material prediction
claims.source: Vema et al., Supplementary Eqs. S19-S25; eta introduced here as effective capture-and-blocking fraction
assumptions: same critical gap and creep law
costs: eta, f, and geometry must be independently acquired; nonzero initial coverage needs Eq. S25 correction
claims.falsifier: Failure of measured critical capacity to scale with captured fraction under controlled matched conditions rejects this simplified transfer.
claims.next_gate: Measure eta and validate on held-out pressure/current conditions.

claims.exact_statement: Fu et al. report Mg metal coating dissolving in molten Li and diffusing into bulk Li with low, stable Li|garnet resistance; this is a chemistry-specific counterexample to inferring insoluble insulating behavior from Mg identity alone, not a prediction for LaMg3.
claims.source: Fu et al., Angew. Chem. 2017, DOI 10.1002/ange.201708637
assumptions: published abstract description of Mg coating experiment
costs: different phase, processing, and alloy composition from LiMgLa
claims.falsifier: Not applicable to LiMgLa; direct phase-specific data would determine its behavior.

claims.exact_statement: A pressure/current-dependent Vema-like capacity penalty from Mg/La inoculant residues in LiMgLa|LLZTO is a falsifiable candidate mechanism, but no numeric safe-capacity bound or validated tradeoff follows from the inspected source evidence.
claims.source: Synthesis of Ji, Vema, and Fu primary sources
assumptions: Mg/La-bearing phase may persist and become an interfacial transport bottleneck
costs: phase and volume-fraction characterization, capture mass balance, Li+ transport, creep, matched cells, cryo microscopy, impedance, and pressure/current series
claims.falsifier: No Mg-bearing enrichment or no incremental predictive value after controlling for initial impedance/current localization/pressure rejects this mechanism for the protocol.
claims.next_gate: Run the matched Li / Li-Mg / Li-Mg-La experiment with interrupted chemistry maps and held-out pressure/current prediction.
